content:
Apple's stock price dropped significantly after the WWDC keynote, with some attributing this to market disappointment over the company's AI announcements.

While we don't necessarily agree with that analysis, investors now seem quite welcoming of the company's cautious stance on AI spending, with shares rebounding 15% from their June lows...

The stock price fell 4% the day after the keynote, though multiple macroeconomic factors were weighing on a basket of stocks at the time, including US military strikes against Iran after a helicopter was shot down.

It has since rebounded even more, once again approaching record highs. Bloomberg sees AI as one of the factors at play, though somewhat indirectly. It points out that investors are increasingly concerned about AI spending at other companies, and Apple's relatively cautious approach is now being seen as an advantage.

Apple's stock reversal reflects growing market unease over whether massive AI spending will pay off, and despite its own AI products repeatedly disappointing investors, Apple's decision not to take part in the data center arms race is increasingly being viewed as an asset rather than a liability. "There is a tug of war going on in the market, and Apple is benefiting right now because it isn't in the middle of the AI trade," said Mark Bronzo, chief investment strategist at Rye Strategic Partners. "People are worried about what kind of return the hyperscalers are going to get from AI spending...

Analysts reportedly aren't worried that the company's price hikes could dent demand, and are welcoming its decision to defend margins. JPMorgan says past price increases haven't significantly impacted demand, and is optimistic about the potential revenue from a possible iPhone Ultra.

While this might be overly optimistic, there does seem to be a broad consensus that Apple's finances are heading in the right direction, with net income expected to grow 17% this fiscal year.
